h1: The 6 Best Carpet Cleaners for Area Rugs, from Spot Machines to Uprights, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Carpet Cleaners for Area Rugs: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 carpet cleaners for area rugs from Bissell, Hoover, Shark and Vacmaster, covering uprights and portable spot machines.
summary: The BISSELL TurboClean Upright is the best carpet cleaner for area rugs of any real size, because an upright covers a 5 by 8 rug in a few passes. The Hoover PowerDash Pet is the best compact machine for pet owners, the BISSELL Little Green is the classic spot cleaner for small rugs and stains, and the Shark StainStriker handles stubborn marks. The Vacmaster is the lowest-cost portable entry.
intro: The first question to ask about an area rug is not which machine to buy but what the rug is made of. Wool, silk and some hand-knotted pieces can bleed dye or shrink when wet, while a synthetic polypropylene rug will happily take a hot-water wash. A powerful extractor in the wrong hands can ruin a rug that no machine could replace.

This ranking assumes you have checked the care label and will be cleaning durable synthetic or machine-made rugs. We reviewed six carpet cleaners from their listings, from uprights to portable spot machines, and ranked them on coverage, handling and how well each suits rug-sized jobs. The listings carry few numbers, so we rely on category knowledge and flag the gaps.

products.name: BISSELL TurboClean Upright Carpet Cleaner
products.verdict: An upright machine with the cleaning path to cover a full-size rug without endless passes.
products.description:
The TurboClean is a BISSELL upright carpet cleaner in the $100 to $200 bracket. Where portable machines work in small patches, an upright has a wide head that cleans a stripe at a time and a larger tank that lasts through a whole room.

It wins because rugs are broad, flat surfaces, and a full-size machine does them faster and more evenly than a hand tool. The upright format also gives you walking height, so you are not bent over a hose for an hour. On the other hand, it is bulky to store and heavier than portable units, and it cannot reach stair edges or tight corners the way a hand tool can.

Buy it if you have several large rugs or a living room full of them. Skip it if your rugs are small and your storage is tight.
pros: Wide head covers big rugs fast
products.idealFor: Homes with several large synthetic rugs.
products.skipIf: You have small rugs and tight storage.

products.name: Hoover PowerDash Pet Compact Carpet Cleaner Machine
products.verdict: A compact machine tuned for pet messes, small enough for a closet shelf.
products.description:
The PowerDash Pet is Hoover's compact carpet cleaner, listed as portable and priced in the $100 to $200 bracket. The pet name signals a design aimed at urine, muddy paws and hair, which are the usual reasons people clean an area rug.

Second place reflects a sensible trade. It is far easier to store than the upright and quicker to set up for a single rug by the door. The compact body does, however, mean smaller tanks and more refills when you tackle a large rug, and it takes longer per square foot than the TurboClean. For a rug under about 5 by 8 feet it is a strong fit.

Choose it for homes with dogs or cats and a few mid-size rugs. Skip it if your rugs are very large and you want faster coverage.
products.idealFor: Pet owners with a few mid-size rugs.

products.name: BISSELL Little Green Multi-Purpose Portable Carpet Cleaner
products.verdict: The classic hand-tool spot cleaner, ideal for stains on small rugs and runners.
products.description:
The Little Green is a portable cleaner in the $50 to $100 bracket, built around a hose and a hand tool for spot work. On a rug it is best used for stains, edges and small pieces that you can lift onto a hard floor.

Third place fits the tool's strengths. It is cheap, light and gets into corners and fringe edges that an upright cannot, and it does nothing to make a whole room cleaner quickly. A full-size rug takes many small passes, and each refill interrupts the job. That is why it sits below the machines that are designed for coverage.

It is the right buy for small rugs, runners and accident clean-ups. Skip it if you want to clean several large rugs in one afternoon.
products.idealFor: Small rugs, runners and spot cleaning.
products.skipIf: You clean big rugs in one session.

products.name: Shark StainStriker Portable Carpet/Upholstery Cleaner
products.verdict: A portable cleaner aimed at tough stains, useful on rugs and furniture alike.
products.description:
The StainStriker is Shark's portable carpet and upholstery cleaner, listed in the $100 to $200 bracket. It is built to work harder on old marks, and its upholstery use means the same machine can freshen a sofa.

Fourth place sits between spot work and full coverage. It beats the Little Green on stain power, but like any portable machine it remains slow across a large rug, so it is not the first choice for coverage. The higher price also overlaps with the Hoover and TurboClean, which suit rugs better, and that squeezes its value for a rug-only buyer.

Buy it if you have both stained rugs and upholstered furniture to tackle. Skip it if rugs are your only target and you want faster coverage.
products.idealFor: Owners with stained rugs and furniture.

products.name: Vacmaster 400 Series Portable Carpet & Upholstery Spot Cleaner Machine
products.verdict: A budget portable spot cleaner for carpet and upholstery in the $50 to $100 range.
products.description:
The Vacmaster 400 Series is a portable carpet and upholstery spot cleaner in the $50 to $100 bracket. Vacmaster is better known for wet-dry shop vacuums than for rug care, and the listing offers few details.

Fifth place is about information and track record. As a spot machine it does the same job as the Little Green, with fewer proven accessories and a less established support network behind it. If the price is lower and you only need to treat the odd stain on a rug, that can be acceptable, but the listing gives no tank size or suction to compare.

Pick it if you want a low-cost spot cleaner for occasional use. Skip it if you want guaranteed parts availability or a larger machine.
products.idealFor: Occasional stain treatment on a budget.
products.skipIf: You want proven parts and support.

products.name: BISSELL Little Green Mini Portable Carpet Cleaner
products.verdict: The smallest machine here, handy for doormats, bath rugs and tiny stains.
products.description:
The Little Green Mini is a compact portable cleaner in the $50 to $100 bracket, and it is the smallest machine in this ranking. It takes the spot-cleaning idea down to a size that can live in a closet or under a sink.

Last place is a fair reflection of its role. Very small rugs, doormats and bath mats suit it well, and it makes quick work of a single stain. A real area rug, even a modest 4 by 6, is beyond its comfortable range because the small tank forces constant refilling. It sits just below the Vacmaster since the larger machines give you more per pass.

Buy it for tiny rugs and quick stain jobs. Skip it if your rugs are large or you want a general-purpose cleaner.
cons: Tank too small for larger rugs
products.idealFor: Doormats, bath rugs and tiny stains.
products.skipIf: Your rugs are 4 by 6 feet or larger.

whatMatters.detail: Synthetic and many machine-made rugs tolerate extraction, but wool, silk and hand-knotted rugs can shrink, bleed or lose shape. Check the care tag, and test cleaning solution on a hidden corner. When in doubt, a professional is cheaper than a ruined rug.

Uprights clean a wide stripe and suit large rugs, while portable spot machines use a hose and are best for stains and small pieces. Decide whether you need coverage or precision. Many households end up with one of each.

Rug cleaning uses water quickly, so a small tank means many trips to the sink. A compact tank keeps the machine light, but it will slow a large job. Match the tank to the biggest rug you plan to clean.

whatMatters.factor: Drying time and moisture left behind
whatMatters.detail: A rug that stays wet can smell musty and may leave marks on the floor beneath it. Extraction power decides how dry the rug ends up. Lift the rug off the floor or use fans, and avoid putting it back until it is dry to the touch.

Pet-focused machines usually include a tool or formula for urine and odors. Check which cleaning solutions the machine accepts and avoid mixing brands. Treat fresh stains quickly for the best results.

faq.q: Can I use a carpet cleaner on a wool area rug?
faq.a: Only if the care label allows it. Wool can shrink or bleed when soaked, so many makers advise professional cleaning. Test any solution on a hidden spot and keep water use low.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake with rug cleaning?
faq.a: Using too much water and letting the rug stay wet. This can leave musty smells, mildew and stains on the floor beneath. Extract thoroughly and dry the rug completely.

faq.q: Is the upright worth it over a portable?
faq.a: For rugs of 5 by 8 feet or more, yes, because it saves a lot of time and effort. For small rugs and stains, a portable such as the Little Green is easier to handle and store.

faq.q: How do I prepare a rug for cleaning?
faq.a: Vacuum both sides to lift loose dirt, then move furniture off the rug. Check the care label and test the solution on a corner. If you can, clean it on a hard surface outdoors.

faq.q: How do I dry a rug after cleaning?
faq.a: Hang it over a rack or raise it off the floor so air reaches the back. Use fans or open windows to speed it up. Do not replace it over a damp floor.
Fringe can tangle in brushes, so use a hand tool on the edges of a rug. Portable machines are better here than uprights. Comb the fringe gently when it dries.

finalTake: For large rugs, the BISSELL TurboClean Upright is the best carpet cleaner here, thanks to its wide cleaning path and a tank that suits big jobs. The Hoover PowerDash Pet is the better choice for pet homes with mid-size rugs, while the Little Green is the dependable spot cleaner. Always check the care label first. A good machine only helps if the rug can handle the water.
